Case No.276 of 2022 pending before the learned // 2 // S.D.J.M., Panposh, Rourkela for commission of alleged offences under sections 408/ 419/ 420/ 467/ 468/ 506/ 34 of the Indian Penal Code.

sentences.text: When the matter was taken up on 02.02.2024, learned counsel for the State not only filed the detailed investigation report but also took time to obtain instruction on the affidavit filed on behalf of the petitioners dated 04.08.2023.

It is mentioned in paragraphs-8 & 9 of the anticipatory bail application that despite the demand of the Government to clear the dues, the Brahmani Engicon Private Ltd. (herein after "the Company")
failed to comply with the statutory demands in time and the informant Kamalpat Dalmia, who was dealing with the financial aspect and was also authorized to sign cheques and transfer of funds against the outstanding in the market, did not cooperate and release the payment.

Since the Company failed to pay the labour charges, notice was received by the Company from the Joint Labour Commissioner, Rourkela and owing to such demand of the statutory authority, the petitioner no.1 was constrained to open a separate account in the name of the Company in ICICI Bank.

It is further stated that out of Rs.50.00 lakh received from the Government, payments were made to different creditors through bank by way of account transfer and some amount has also been paid in cash through cash withdrawal from the bank to the labourers at different sites, which was paid under due process.

It is further stated that the allegations made by the informant that the petitioners misappropriated // 3 // and syphoned the money of the Company is out and out false and that the petitioners have not withdrawn a single pie from the Company's account for personal use.

Mr. Jagannath Pattnaik, learned Senior Advocate for the petitioner drew the attention of this Court to Annexure-5 series, which is the statement of account of the ICICI Bank, which indicates that Rs.50.00 lakh came to the account of the Company on 30.12.2021 and thereafter on the next day,
i.e., 31.12.2021, there has been a cash withdrawal of Rs.5.00 lakh and then on different dates, there has been online account transfer of different amount to the tune of Rs.21.00 lakh and it is stated that the balance amount, which was there in the account of the company in ICICI Bank, i.e.,
Rs,24.00 lakh was seized by the Police during course of investigation.

Learned counsel for the State was asked to obtain instruction as to whether the ground taken and the argument advanced by the learned counsel for the petitioners regarding payment of Rs.26.00 lakh and odd to different creditors is correct or not.

Today learned counsel for the State has produced the written instruction received from the Inspector- in-charge, Raghunathpalli Police Station to the effect that after verification of affidavit filed by the petitioners regarding payment of Rs.26.00 lakh and odd to the creditors.
It is found to be correct but out of which the petitioners have withdrawn the cash of Rs.5.00 lakh, which could not be proved regarding payment towards the creditors.

Since the online transfer of Rs.21.00 lakh was found to be correct and the documents relating to payment of Rs.5.00 lakh to different persons by way of debit vouchers having filed, copies of which have been // 4 // served on the learned counsel for the State, in which the signatures of the concerned persons, who have received the case, are there, the Investigating Officer is free to examine those persons and verify whether the debit vouchers are genuine or not, whether the persons have received such amount or not and if so, for what purpose and whether the same has got any connection with the Company or not.
The written instruction received from the Inspector-in-charge, Raghunathpalli Police Station is taken on record.

sentences.text: Mr. Jagannath Pattnaik, learned Senior Advocate for the petitioners submitted that the petitioners are ready and willing to cooperate with the investigating agency in respect for verification of the debit vouchers and they will also appear as and when there is notice from the Investigating Officer to that effect fixing the date and time of appearance.
Mr. S. Mishra, learned counsel for the informant opposed the prayer for bail.

Considering the submissions made by the learned counsel for the respective parties, after going through the averments taken in this anticipatory bail application, the affidavit and the documents filed and the instruction obtained by the learned counsel for the State, I am inclined to release the petitioners on anticipatory bail and accordingly, this Court directs that in the event of arrest of the petitioners in connection with the aforesaid case, they shall be released on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs.10,000/- (rupees ten thousand) each with two sureties each for the like amount to the satisfaction of the arresting officer with further conditions that on receipt of the notice, they shall cooperate with the // 5 // investigating agency, shall appear before the Investigating Officer as and when necessary and shall not tamper with the evidence.
Violation of any of the above conditions shall entail cancellation of bail.
The ABLAPL is accordingly disposed of.
Issue urgent certified copy as per Rules.
( S.K. Sahoo) Judge M.K.Rout Sudhanshu Sekhar vs State Of Odisha .... Opp.
